newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar appoints three banks as brokers for bourse.
newsitem.headline: Qatar appoints three banks as brokers for bourse.

text.p: Qatar on Monday moved a step closer towards opening an official bourse by appointing three commercial banks as brokers, officials said.
"Qatar National Bank, Doha Bank Ltd and the Commercial Bank of Qatar have been chosen as authorised brokers for the Doha Securities Market (DSM)," an official said.

"Three more brokers from outside the banking sector will be appointed, but their selection will take some time, because we have asked some 20 firms which have applied for the job to form three credible joint ventures by May 15," he said.
The official said the formal bourse would become operational in the fourth week of May.

"The Minister of Finance, Economy and Trade, His Excellency Sheikh Mohammad bin Khalifa al-Thani, has been requested to open the floor officially any day between May 25-28, depending on his convenience," he said.
At present investors trade the shares of 18 companies on the telephone through some banks or private brokers. The official bourse will operate electronically.
DSM officials expect market capitalisation to rise considerably from the present $1.9 billion after the opening of the official floor.
Initially, only Qatari nationals will be allowed to participate in trading.
"Later, we'll allow GCC nationals and thereafter other foreigners to trade," said Hussein Ali al-Abdullah, general manager and vice-chairman of the DSM.
The GCC -- Gulf Cooperation Council -- groups Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Kuwait, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman.

Proposals are also under consideration to change the face value of shares from 100 riyals at present to 10 riyals. "But in this respect, a decree has to be issued and the boards of companies will have to adjust their books," he said.
